statement: A lemonade stand sells each lemonade for $5. Customers queue up and buy one lemonade each, in the order given by bills, paying with a single $5, $10 or $20 bill.

You start with no money at all, so any change you give must come from bills that earlier customers paid with. Every customer must receive exactly the right change: nothing for $5, $5 back for $10, and $15 back for $20.

Return true if you can give every customer correct change, and false otherwise. Greedily, when making $15 prefer one $10 and one $5 over three $5s, because $5 bills are the only ones that can change a $10.

examples.explanation: After three $5s, the $10 customer gets a $5 back. The $20 customer then gets the $10 and a $5. Everyone was served.
The first customer pays $10 while the till is empty, so there is no $5 to give back.
Both $10 customers take a $5 in change, which leaves two $10s and no $5. The $20 customer needs $15 and it cannot be made.
